newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Bullish naphtha resists crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Bullish naphtha resists crude.

text.p: Naphtha prices held their ground despite weaker crude as Indian tenders illustrated current strong regional fundamentals, while gasoline slipped marginally, traders said on Monday.
Naphtha swaps firmed by up to 20 cents per barrel to $24.00/$24.15 for March, reflecting a recent firming trend.
"As a result, IOC has received better prices," a Japanese trader said on state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) tender results.

IOC sold 30,000 tonnes of high aromatic naphtha (HAN) lifting from Cochin to Swiss trader Glencore at $16.00 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes on a free-on-board (fob) basis, higher than its last HAN export from Cochin, which loaded January 29-31, at a $20.98 discount.
The tender for the cargo lifting from the east coast between March 1-3 closed February 20 and was valid for one day.
In another tender which closed at the same time, IOC sold 25,000 tonnes of natural gas liquids (NGL) to Glencore at $30.75 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes, fob.
A source at Glencore was not able to confirm the award as the company has not received confirmation.

Gasoline was traded between two European traders at $26.60 per barrel fob Singapore lifting March 22-26 for 50,000 barrels of the 95-octane unleaded grade. On Friday, the cargo was last offered at $26.80.
"But fundamentally it is strong in March," said a trader with a major oil company.
Traders said the drop was in line with crude, as supplies were tight ahead of turnarounds in Singapore, China and Japan.
Some reformate was being sought into Japan to cover for the maintenance shutdown at Okinawa, traders said.

But China still had one to two 20,000 tonnes of 90-93-octane unleaded cargoes to sell, lifting in March which it was targetting a premium of more than $2.00 per barrel over the Singpore 92-octane quote, a source said.
